subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics and persisted API shape, and repository policy treats config/default additions as compatibility-sensitive maintainer decisions.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current fixed anchored `every` semantics and close or mark the cron `every` portion as not planned.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron-expression stagger implementation and product-boundary decision are closest to this remaining scheduler API choice.
